visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a wide aerial shot of a mountainous desert landscape displayed on a large curved simulator screen, creating a sense of flight. Chinese and English subtitles appear as overlays at the bottom. The lighting is bright and naturalistic within the projected imagery, while the surrounding room is dimly lit. (2) A selfie medium shot shows a man with long dark hair and a patterned shirt sitting in the dark simulator room. He gazes upward with an expression of awe, his facial features highlighted by the rhythmic flickering light from the screen. He remains seated and still, absorbing the visual experience. (3) A sequence of shots captures the exterior and interior of an 'Attack on Titan' themed attraction. Large posters featuring characters like Eren Yeager and colossal titans decorate the walls. A staff member is seen in the background near a doorway. The lighting is warm and cinematic, emphasizing the themed textures of the walls. (4) The man holds a physical red and black 'Anime Flight Festival' ticket close to the camera lens. The focus is sharp on the printed text of the ticket while the background lobby is softly blurred. His hand is steady as he presents the credential to the viewer. (5) The man poses in a well-lit corridor next to a life-size cardboard cutout of the character Levi Ackerman. He wears a plaid overshirt, a graphic t-shirt, and a black cap. He holds up a peace sign with his fingers while smiling slightly at the camera. (6) A montage features detailed character posters and wall graphics, specifically showing Mikasa Ackerman in her vertical maneuvering equipment and the muscular back of the Attack Titan. Text overlays in Chinese emphasize the intensity of the 3D effects. (7) The man sits on a bench against a bright green screen background. He holds a white comic-style speech bubble prop with Chinese text. He looks towards the camera with a playful expression, adjusting his posture slightly for the photo. (8) Back in the theater, a low-angle shot shows several audience members strapped into mechanical motion seats. The floor features glowing neon blue and red light strips that illuminate the dark, industrial-style interior of the 'flying theater'. (9) A male staff member in a white short-sleeved uniform stands before the audience, performing the 'Survey Corps' salute with his right fist clenched over his heart. His expression is serious and professional under the dim ambient lights. (10) The video ends with a close-up selfie of the man mimicking the salute. He looks directly into the camera with a determined and energetic expression, his face lit by a blue flickering light source that suggests the motion ride has resumed.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The sequence opens with cinematic orchestral music featuring driving string sections and triumphant brass fanfares. A male narrator delivers lines in Japanese with a deep, professional, and dramatic tone, setting a serious mood. No significant SFX are audible over the dense musical arrangement, which maintains a fast, epic tempo throughout the phase. (2) The vlogger's voice enters, speaking Mandarin with moderate speed and high pitch variability, expressing clear excitement about the simulator. The background music ducks slightly to prioritize the speech. A subtle ambient room tone from the theater simulator, including a faint mechanical hum and air conditioning noise, is perceptible in the frequency floor. (3) A sudden vocal transition occurs as a Japanese male voice shouts the iconic command 'Shinzou wo Sasageyo' with high arousal, intense projection, and a sharp pitch contour. Simultaneously, the BGM swells dramatically, introducing a full choir and aggressive electric guitar riffs that mimic the 'Attack on Titan' opening theme's high-energy rock texture. (4) The vlogger repeats the salute command loudly in a shouting voice, matching the high intensity and arousal of the swelling music. The audio track reaches its climax with the high-energy rock theme, characterized by fast-paced drumming, distorted guitars, and a dense, layered spectral profile that fills the entire bandwidth until the video cuts.
